executive_summary: An internal API that stores per-user UI preferences for in-house tools. It lets teams persist settings like default dashboard, theme, and timezone across sessions without building bespoke storage in each tool.
problem_statement: Internal tools each reimplement their own preference storage. Preferences do not carry across tools, onboarding is repetitive, and inconsistent defaults create support churn.
proposed_solution_overview:
Provide a shared preferences API behind API Gateway, backed by DynamoDB, with Cognito-authenticated access scoped to the calling user.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Client --> APIGW[API Gateway]
  APIGW --> Lambda[Preferences Lambda]
  Lambda --> DDB[(DynamoDB)]
```

user_stories.outcome: the same preferences apply when I open another in-house tool

user_stories.action: read and write user preferences through a shared API
user_stories.outcome: I do not reimplement storage in every new tool

user_stories.action: view error rates for the preferences API
user_stories.outcome: I can respond to regressions before they reach users

functional_requirements.description: The system shall return the stored preferences object for the authenticated user on GET /preferences.
functional_requirements.rationale: Tools need a single read endpoint that returns the current preference set.
acceptance_criteria: Given an authenticated user with saved preferences, when the client calls GET /preferences, then the API returns the stored object with HTTP 200.

functional_requirements.description: The system shall upsert preferences for the authenticated user on PUT /preferences.
functional_requirements.rationale: Tools need to persist changes without branching between create and update.
acceptance_criteria: Given an authenticated user, when the client PUTs a valid preferences body, then the API returns HTTP 200 and the next GET reflects the new values.

functional_requirements.description: The system shall reject unauthenticated requests with HTTP 401.
functional_requirements.rationale: Preferences are scoped per user and must not be readable or writable without a valid token.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request without a valid Cognito token, when it reaches the preferences API, then the API returns HTTP 401 without invoking the Lambda handler.

non_functional_requirements.description: GET /preferences p95 latency stays under 150 ms at 50 requests per second.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic 50 rps load test, when it runs for 10 minutes, then the p95 server-side latency stays below 150 ms.

non_functional_requirements.description: All traffic to the preferences API uses TLS 1.2 or higher.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request on HTTP or TLS below 1.2, when it reaches API Gateway, then the request is refused.

technical_context_and_dependencies: Depends on the internal Cognito user pool and the platform DynamoDB account. No new upstream systems introduced.

risks.description: Adoption stalls if only one team integrates the new API.
risks.mitigation: Pilot with two tools in the first milestone and publish a short migration guide.

risks.description: Schema drift if each tool invents its own preference keys.
risks.mitigation: Document a shared preference namespace convention and review PRs that add new keys.

success_metrics.metric: Tools integrated with the preferences API
success_metrics.target_value: 3 tools within one quarter of launch
success_metrics.measurement_method: Manual tracking in the platform team wiki

timeline_and_milestones: M1: API and Lambda in staging. M2: two pilot tools integrated. M3: production rollout.
